text:
OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The launch signaled a shift in frontier reasoning models toward integrating vision directly into the model architecture rather than bolting it on, alongside native tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) that is trained into the model itself [Source: ev-1]. It also marked OpenAI’s first private chain-of-thought policy, where reasoning tokens are not exposed to API callers [Source: ev-1].

Strategically, with GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used this release to defend its position at the reasoning-model frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic's agentic-coding push [Source: ev-1]. The launch reframed frontier capability as "tool-using reasoning at commodity prices," evidenced by o4-mini’s pricing of $1.10 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens, compared to o3’s $10/$40 [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, o3 set a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark, achieving about 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute—matching or exceeding the ~85% human baseline—and becoming the first model to reach this level [Source: ev-1].
